items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: Ray Brown used to tell me, he says, “Well, you know, keep the bass up front... And he says, “You be conscious of how you project your bass line.”

ctx.x: Did that experience with the singer that time find its way into your teaching?

Oh absolutely. That’s where those statements come from of stop leaning on other people to make you sound good. Because that’s what bass players tend to do. And most people say, “Oh I didn’t know a bass could do that.” Well the bass is not doing that, the bass is just a conduit of what the brain is doing, really. But people don’t hear that. I mean the bass is — Ray Brown used to tell me, he says, “Well, you know, keep the bass up front. We know we’re in the back, but the bass is always up front.” And he says, “You…

That’s a great statement. You can put that on your resume. You know it’s such a different thing for a saxophone player, which I play. If you half know a tune you probably can get through it. You can play the melody and then you can listen to the guys do the harmony, and you can get through it. But you guys, you can’t stop concentrating I guess.
